subject.title: Encinitas Union School District Board of Trustees

text: Jillian Cocayne brings real expertise. A district parent with more than 20 years experience in nonpartisan governmental policy across Washington D.C., London, and Brussels. She serves on the Citizens Bond Oversight Committee protecting the $158 million School Bond Measure Z and is a parent representative on the Special Education Parent Council.

Jillian Cocayne will give working parents and special education families a real voice on our board. Over the past two years, she has attended more EUSD public meetings than any other community member — the budget reviews, the curriculum debates, the late-night controversies. She knows this district.
Jillian Cocayne will protect our curriculum from book bans and outside culture wars, so every child and family is welcome, included, and represented in our schools.
Jillian Cocayne will make every dollar count, focusing spending on teachers and students while fighting for fairer funding at every level of government.
Jillian Cocayne will open the lines of communication, serving as a bridge between families and the district — no more black box.
Jillian Cocayne is endorsed by Congressman Mike Levin, state and local elected officials, community organizations, and the Teachers of Encinitas.
For more information, please visit: jillian4eusd.com

text: Proudly endorsed by the Teachers of Encinitas!
I’ve been a teacher, vice principal and principal at schools across San Diego. I hold a master’s degree in curriculum and instruction and researched student assessment systems at Harvard.
All five of my grandchildren attend EUSD schools and I’m running because three specific problems need fixing.

First, I will push for a unified, grade level curriculum across every EUSD school. In the last 10 years, EUSD has seen a five percent drop in math and reading scores across grade levels. Without a shared curriculum, students in different classrooms learn different things, creating gaps as they advance. Second, I want to institute a district-wide policy limiting the use of tech in classrooms. Currently, technology use is up to the teacher’s discretion and may be used in place of instruction. Overreliance on tablets and devices hurts students’ ability to read, focus, and think critically. Third, I want to ensure the district uses the current budget surplus to address gaps in student achievement.
I humbly ask for your vote.
https://www.hargrave4eusd.net

text: As a Special Education employee and a parent of two children in EUSD, I see the importance of our schools from both the classroom and family perspectives.

Our schools should return to academic excellence. Children rise to the expectations we set for them, and schools should maintain high academic and behavioral standards that help every student succeed.

Strong schools are built on strong partnerships with parents. When families and educators work together, students thrive. Parents build the foundation of character and responsibility, while teachers educate, challenge, and inspire. District leadership should strengthen trust between parents and educators.

Smaller, well-supported classrooms allow teachers to know each child, build meaningful relationships, and meet individual needs. We can pursue smaller class sizes while remaining responsible stewards of taxpayer dollars.

As an immigrant with experience in different educational systems, I bring a broad perspective and deep appreciation for the opportunities our Encinitas schools provide. EUSD should prepare students to think critically, work hard, act with integrity, and overcome life’s challenges.
As a school board member, I will approach every decision with an unwavering commitment to what is best for students.
It would be an honor to serve our students, families, and community.

text: As a parent, educator, and lifelong public servant, I believe every child deserves the opportunity to succeed in a safe, supportive, and academically excellent school.

For more than 30 years, I have proudly served the Encinitas community and most recently as the Deputy Fire Chief for the Encinitas Fire Department. This role has entrusted me with leading emergency operations, managing public resources, developing future leaders, and making difficult decisions with integrity, accountability, fiscal responsibility, and teamwork. Every decision I make is guided by what is best for the community.

Education has also been a meaningful part of my life. As an adjunct instructor at Miramar College, I teach and mentor future firefighters, reinforcing the importance of strong educational foundations, high expectations, and dedicated teachers who prepare s tudents for lifelong success.

As a parent, I understand families want schools where children are supported academically by exceptional educators and prepared for the future. Parents should be respected as partners, with transparency, communication, and responsible governance guiding district decisions.
Encinitas has given so much to my family over the years. Serving on the Encinitas Union School District Board would be another opportunity to give back to the community that I am proud of.

text: Our Encinitas and La Costa K-6 public schools are very good, and I’ll work hard to make them even better. I believe in public education because I’ve lived its promise: child of immigrants, native Californian, product of California public schools that carried me to Stanford and a business career.

As an EUSD parent of three, I know that our kids need excellent teachers, safe classrooms, and a thoughtful approach to technology. I’ll champion a districtwide tech audit, no iPads in K-2, and phased technology use in upper grades. Screens should support learning, not replace it.

As an experienced independent and nonprofit board member, I’ll bring fiscal discipline to every budget decision, and I’ll prioritize hiring teachers, aides, and specialists. I’ll always listen to parents and teachers, because the best ideas come from our classrooms.
My community commitment runs deep: PTA board member, School Site Council member, Coastal Roots Farm board member, and Chair of Measure Z (Stronger Schools for EUSD).
I’m endorsed by the Teachers of Encinitas, Congressman Mike Levin, and the Sierra Club, and a Moms Demand Action Gun Sense Candidate.
I’m asking for your vote to make our EUSD schools even better.
Thank you,
Bill Shen
